Mac daily-driver review.
Signed content-viewport evidence.

This report is a screen-by-screen review of the Wilted Mac app as built from the candidate commit below. Every image is an app-owned, window-scoped capture of the Wilted process itself, taken during a signed local XCUITest session. It is candidate evidence for owner review. It is not owner acceptance, not a release record, and not evidence of any production, device, or store state.

2. Method and evidence labels

Pixels come from XCUIElement.screenshot() scoped to the Wilted app's own window. Nothing in this session captured the screen, the desktop, or another application's window. XCTest's automatic whole-screen recording is disabled at the project level — the generated scheme carries systemAttachmentLifetime = "keepNever", so no full-screen recording was written to disk or retained.

Evidence typeRequired proofLimit
Exact processFresh signed app bundle identity, signature authority, team, and launched PID.Does not establish release status.
Accessibility treeAttached macOS Accessibility hierarchy bound to the exact process, including route and control identifiers.Interaction inventory, not pixels.
Content viewportXCUIElement.screenshot() on the app's own window, paired with a geometry sidecar written from inside the process at geometry-scope=NSApp.mainWindow.contentView. The sidecar records content-bounds equal to the window frame, which is what makes a window-scoped screenshot a content-viewport screenshot.The content view is full-size and extends under the unified titlebar (content-layout-rect is 900x398 against 900x450 bounds), so window chrome is composited over the content viewport and is visible in every frame. Anything the app scrolls below the visible fold is not in the pixels.
Source inventoryShipping-view controls and system handoff descriptions.Not runtime or visual evidence.

Resolution and crop

The capture hook parks the window on the highest-backingScaleFactor attached display before any frame is taken, so evidence is Retina-native rather than dependent on where macOS restored the window. At backing-scale=2.0 a 900x450 window is expected-pixels=1800x900, which is what the sidecars record. Every embedded PNG is 1768x868 because a uniform 8pt (16px) inset is removed from each edge: 1800−32=1768 and 900−32=868. The inset exists because the window's rounded corners are partly transparent, and the compositor fills that alpha with whatever is behind the window — one uncropped frame contained readable fragments of an unrelated desktop window at the top-left corner. The inset removes that region on all four edges. It is the only modification made to any frame.

3. Onboarding and first run

Wilted has no account creation, sign-in, or welcome sequence. First run opens directly on Larder with the composer and an empty saved list; the app is usable without configuring anything. The idle frame in section 4 is therefore also the first-run frame in every respect except that its fixture has content saved. Sync is opt-in and lives in Settings; it is not part of first run and does not gate any other surface.

No separate onboarding screen exists in this build, so none is captured. If one is added, this report must be refreshed.

4. Larder

Larder is the primary library destination and the default route at launch. The sidebar (wilted-mac-sidebar) holds the wordmark and the three destinations: wilted-navigation-library, wilted-navigation-processor, and wilted-navigation-settings. The detail pane is wilted-mac-library-detail.

Per-item controls carry a stable content hash in their identifier: wilted-article-row-item-<hash> and wilted-episode-row-item-<hash> for the rows, with wilted-article-actions-item-<hash> and wilted-episode-actions-item-<hash> for their action menus. Ordering is exposed through wilted-library-order. These identifiers are present in the attached Accessibility tree for every captured route.

5. Always-visible bottom rail

The retained product direction is an always-visible bottom rail. Bottom is the accepted placement. The rail is present in idle and in playback, on every destination, and there is no separate Now Playing tab. Playback adds current-item state plus inline Transcript and Up Next expansion within the same rail.

Keyboard transports are exposed as wilted-player-keyboard-transports, and audio route recovery as wilted-player-route-recovery. Both are in the attached Accessibility tree for the playback routes.

6. Prep

Prep is a primary destination reached from wilted-navigation-processor; its detail pane is wilted-mac-processor-detail.

7. Settings

Settings is a primary destination reached from wilted-navigation-settings; its pane is wilted-mac-settings. It holds the sync surface (wilted-sync-controls) with wilted-sync-status, wilted-sync-detail, wilted-sync-producer-identity, wilted-sync-last-fetch, wilted-sync-last-send, wilted-sync-refresh, and wilted-sync-upload.

8. Download and recovery states

Two disabled/recovery states are captured from fixtures that force the failure rather than simulating it in the report.

9. Roles and permission differences

Wilted Mac has no user roles, no sign-in, and no per-user authorization surface, so there are no role-dependent routes or controls to show. The only permission-shaped variation is iCloud account availability, which changes the Settings sync surface and is captured in frame 8.2. The app requests no microphone, camera, location, or Screen Recording permission, and this capture session triggered no system permission prompt.

10. System-owned boundaries

Finder is the inventoried system-owned handoff for a retained recovery copy. No Finder window was entered during this session, and no Finder, permission prompt, account picker, browser, or desktop surface appears in any embedded frame — by construction, since every frame is scoped to the Wilted window and the 8pt inset removes the transparent corner region where background pixels could otherwise show through. A future Finder interaction must be recorded as a separate, separately labelled system-boundary observation.

11. Coverage limits

These are the parts of the walkthrough this evidence does not cover. They are listed rather than omitted.

  • Below the visible fold. The window is 900x450. The Up Next queue list, the wilted-sync-use-current-account recovery affordance, and the not-ready article row are each present in the attached Accessibility tree for their route but render below the fold, so they are not in the pixels. Their presence is an Accessibility-tree observation, not a visual one.
  • Not-ready article state. A ninth frame was captured for the preparing-article fixture and is deliberately not embedded: at this window size its visible region is indistinguishable from the idle Larder frame, because the not-ready row itself is below the fold. Embedding it would have labelled a state the image does not show.
  • Active preparation progress. No fixture sets an in-flight preparation, so the Prep progress and cancellation states cannot be reached from a test and are not pixel-evidenced. Frame 6.1 shows Prep without an active run.
  • Startup recovery. The startup recovery screen requires the local library store to fail to open. No fixture forces that, so it is not reachable from a capture test and is not evidenced.
  • Not exercised in pixels. Offline-cached state, item removal, search, relaunch continuity, and a successful retry are described by control inventory only. No frame here asserts any of them.

13. Owner acceptance checklist

  1. Review Larder, Prep, and Settings with the always-visible bottom rail present in idle and in playback (frames 4.1, 5.1, 6.1, 7.1).
  2. Review the playback transport inventory, inline Transcript and Up Next expansion, and Escape collapse with focus return (frames 5.1–5.3).
  3. Review the download failure and retry affordance and the sync quarantine recovery state (frames 8.1–8.2).
  4. Read section 11 and decide whether the uncovered states — active preparation, startup recovery, Offline cached, removal, search, relaunch continuity — need evidence before acceptance, or whether a larger capture window is warranted so below-fold content is visible.
  5. Review Finder only as a separately labelled system boundary, and return acceptance or feedback.

Any user-visible route, control, state, copy, or system-boundary change requires another evidence refresh.
